title: Add JSONSchema response_format strict mode + improved error messages (OpenAI compat)
author: Asha Patel
ci_checks: integration-tests: flaky on first run, passed after rerun
description: Adds a strict mode for JSONSchema-based response_format, improves validation error messages, and wires the behavior into the OpenAI compatibility layer. Motivation: customers rely on structured output for downstream parsing and want deterministic server-side validation to catch regressions early. This change implements server-side validation after model output but before responding to the SDK/API client when response_format specifies a JSONSchema and strict=true. Key behaviors: 1) When strict=true the platform validates model-generated JSON against the provided schema. If validation succeeds the parsed object is returned in the standard response envelope. 2) If validation fails, the response contains a structured error payload (response_format_error) with machine-readable validation errors and a concise human message. The error payload follows the OpenAI-compat response_format error conventions used in previous PRs. 3) Streaming behavior: validation is performed after the stream completes; for streaming use-cases we continue to stream tokens but append a final validation result metadata event so clients can safely detect strict-mode failures. 4) Backwards compatibility: strict is opt-in; default behavior unchanged. Contents: implementation in server/validation/jsonschema_validator.go, integration with the OpenAI-compat normalizer in openai_compat/response_normalizer.go, API surface changes in server/api/response_format.go, test coverage in tests/integration/test_jsonschema_strict.py, docs updates in docs/api/response_format.md. Checklist: - [x] Implement JSONSchema validator with AJV-compatible rules and custom format hooks - [x] Add strict-mode flag on response_format and propagate through request/response lifecycle - [x] Produce machine-readable error payload with error codes, JSON path, and short human message - [x] Ensure streaming still functions and emits final validation metadata event - [x] Add unit and integration tests covering valid, invalid, and edge-case schemas - [x] Docs and changelog entry - [x] Add OpenAI-compat normalization and mapping for existing clients

changed_snippet: // server/validation/jsonschema_validator.go: Validate(schema, data) -> (valid bool, errors []ValidationIssue) where ValidationIssue contains code, path, and message. The validator uses a fast path for simple schemas and falls back to AJV-like engine for complex keywords.
review_conversation: Drew: Suggests clearer error codes for distinction between syntactic JSON errors vs schema semantic errors. Liang: Requests streaming metadata event so clients can detect validation failures without waiting for timeout. Evelyn: Asks for explicit test for large arrays and $ref resolution. Author (Asha): Responds that syntactic JSON errors are returned with code 'response_format.json_invalid', schema semantic errors use 'response_format.schema_mismatch' and included path; streaming metadata event implemented as 'validation_result' event appended to stream; added integration tests for large arrays and $ref resolution using mocked resolver. CI initially failed integration-tests on first run due to nondeterministic ordering in error lists; fixed by normalizing errors to deterministic sort. All reviewers approved after fixes.
release_notes: Added 'strict' option to response_format when using JSONSchema. When strict=true the server validates generated JSON and returns a structured error payload on validation failures. Streaming responses now emit a final 'validation_result' metadata event. Backwards compatible since strict is opt-in.
